text:
Aaron: quick sync — ran ACME pilot load this morning, 30m steady. need to lock p95/p99 commitments for sales tomorrow. pasting a short profiler dump and KV hit stats.

Kevin: profiler summary (microbatch, p95, p99, qps, notes):
```
mb=1  p95=180ms p99=420ms  qps=320  kernel=matmul_v2 (good for long seq)
mb=4  p95=210ms p99=620ms  qps=1100 kernel=matmul_v2 (batching increases throughput, tail regresses)
mb=8  p95=260ms p99=920ms  qps=2000 kernel=fused_unfused (cache pressure spikes)
KV hits (steady): 86% warm, cold tail -> p99 spikes ~200-300ms when segfault-like misses
Observations: kernel selector picks fused path for batched short seqs; fused path has higher tail variance on our GPU kernels.
```

Jen: saw a perf regression after PR 0a3f2b4 (kernel selector tweak). p99 went +18% on microbatch=4 runs. suspect heuristic threshold changed from 32->16 tokens so we hit a slower kernel for many requests.

Aaron: exact ask from sales: customer wants p95<200ms and p99<450ms for their tier. can we promise? if not, what tradeoffs/options?

Sam (sales): acme says they need a contractual p99 for key routes. they also expect peak qps bursts. would prefer a configuration we can guarantee with an SLA.

Maria: from product: two suggested options to offer to customer —
- Option A (standard guarantee): p95<220ms, p99<600ms, documented warmup 5m, microbatch default=4.
- Option B (premium): p95<150ms, p99<400ms, require dedicated pool + kv prewarm + microbatch=1 or autotune.
Which is realistic?

Kevin: tradeoffs short: microbatch=1 -> better tail, lower qps; microbatch=4 -> 3-4x throughput, worse p99 unless KV warm / kernel tuned. Kernel swap: forcing matmul_v1 for short sequences reduced p99 by ~120ms in experiments but dropped throughput ~15%.

Jen: regression plan: bisect PRs touching selector heuristics. I can revert the 0a3f2b4 change in a canary and re-run 30m test. If revert fixes p99 we can ship a patch.

Kevin: mitigation plan for sales call: two layers — infra: dedicate N GPUs (reduces scheduling variance), runtime: force kernel hint + aggressive KV prewarm for their routes for first 10 minutes of traffic. Combined should get us close to Option B for steady traffic.

Sam (sales): can we write that as a carve-out: SLA p95 committed, p99 committed if dedicated pool + prewarm configured (add-on)? customer likely to accept. Need wording for contract.

Aaron: risks: cold KV and short-sequence kernel variance are main culprits. We can guarantee p95 easily for most configs. p99 needs either lower microbatch or dedicated pool + prewarm + kernel hint. Also watch perf regression from selector change.

Maria: OK — product wants draft SLO matrix for legal + sales: default tier (sane defaults), enterprise tier (dedicated + prewarm). Maria: can we get numbers by EOD?

Kevin: I'll run a 1h sustained test with: microbatch=1, mb=4, and mb=1+kernel-hint for the customer's route. Will include KV prewarm script (cold->warm). ETA 3h.

Jen: I'll bisect the selector change and put up a revert PR if it correlates. ETA 2h.

Aaron: action items: Kevin -> run tests and post logs; Jen -> bisect/revert if needed; Aaron -> draft SLO matrix and contract language + mitigation notes for Sam.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/runtime-selector-revert -> staging at 1854321200

Sam (sales): thanks — I'll hold off official promise until we get Kevin's numbers. if we can hit Option B with dedicated pool + prewarm, i'll push that as an add-on.

Kevin: quick note — for the 1h run I'll collect p50/p95/p99, kernel hist, KV hit timeline, and GPU util samples every 10s. will paste results in this thread.

Aaron: thanks team. small note for the follow-up call: prepare recommended microbatch defaults per customer profile (low-latency vs high-throughput).

Jen: +1.

Sam (sales): ping me when results are up, will prepare contract draft.

Kevin: starting tests now.
